segments.title: Chương 146: 0146【Thành công và sự chú ý của tư bản】
segments.content:
Three-line poems really took off.

Xici Hutong reacted the fastest. While users were spontaneously writing three-line poems, it seized the opportunity to launch the "Three-Line Love Letter Confession Campaign."

This website often held events, and what's more, they would often connect online activities with offline ones.

They had organized all sorts of strange events, like the "Aigo Cup CS Tournament," "Mask Graffiti to Fight SARS," "Love on the Scene Offline Salon," and so on.

This time, they used three-line poems to create an online dating speed-matching event.

Soon after, the "Wuwen Nongmo" (Playing with Ink and Words) section of the Tianya Club forum also began to solicit three-line poems and even announced plans to contact a publisher for a "Collection of Three-Line Poems."

Next was NGA, right when the closed beta for "World of Warcraft" had just started.

But the number of beta spots was limited, and countless players were bored to tears from waiting. They idled away their days chatting on the forums and decided to start a "World of Warcraft Three-Line Poem" event.

The results were all in this kind of tone: "The refresh key has been pressed until sparks fly,

My inbox remains as cold as ice.

The distance between you and Azeroth is the thickness of one activation code."

Gradually, traditional media began to report on it.

When some organizations were holding events, the planners, looking for a shortcut, simply transplanted the three-line poem idea and, quite unexpectedly, it was widely acclaimed.

Over at Tencent, QQ Zone was about to begin its closed beta, and even the "Hero's Invitation" (invitation codes) had been sent out.

The project team was called "Zone Nest," and its head, Zheng Zhiwu, was meticulously analyzing Xiaonei's recent operation.

Zheng Zhiwu called a meeting with his team members and said, "Our QQ Zone will start its closed beta in one week. As for how to operate it, our initial idea was to imitate MSN Spaces. But MSN Spaces isn't very popular. Instead, the recently rising Xiaonei is worth learning from."

QQ was currently in a state of fierce competition with MSN. Whatever product MSN had, QQ would follow suit with.

QQ Zone was also this kind of imitation product.

"Xiaonei has features that MSN Spaces doesn't. Some of them, I believe, can be adopted by QQ Zone..."

"Let's analyze Xiaonei's recent event again."

"Why did Xiaonei's event focus on story relays, when there were clearly three-line poems? Can anyone answer that for me?"

Tang Daosheng, who had just joined the company this year and was in charge of QQ Zone's monetization, raised his hand.

Zheng Zhiwu said, "Please, go ahead."

Tang Daosheng said, "Although three-line poems can quickly attract a large number of users, the hype comes and goes quickly. The campus love story relay, on the other hand, can last for a long time. It can continuously generate stories, keeping a portion of users engaged."

"Moreover, regardless of whether a user's continuation of the story is selected by Xiaonei, the user will cherish it greatly. They might even continue to serialize it in their own journal, eventually forming their own unique novella. And this novella, in turn, can attract other readers, forming a closed, small circle. The user stickiness of this circle will be greatly increased."

"One novella is one circle, and 100 novellas are a hundred circles. No one can say for sure how many novellas and how many circles Xiaonei's story relay will privately generate."

"Therefore, the event planners at Xiaonei placed more importance on the story relay, using the three-line poems as a supplementary feature."

Hearing this explanation, the others at QQ Zone had a moment of epiphany.

Tang Daosheng had returned to China early this year and was directly appointed as a systems architect. Now he was also on loan, responsible for testing QQ Zone and researching its monetization.

It was inevitable that some people would be unconvinced by this "heavenly demon from beyond the seas" who had parachuted in.

"Mr. Tang's analysis is excellent," Zheng Zhiwu continued. "MSN's management is too institutionalized. After our initial study of them, we should stop paying attention to them and instead learn from more flexible companies. Don't be fooled by MSN's strong momentum now; their product features are already lagging behind QQ, and they haven't been able to keep up with our pace. MSN will be driven out of China sooner or later!"

"From now on, our project members should keep a close eye on Xiaonei. Although our target audiences are slightly different, the content is essentially the same. Whatever new things Xiaonei comes up with, we should analyze them and follow up quickly..."

Shanghai.

Three investment partners from IDG were playing golf.

Xiong Xiaoge, as a founding partner of IDG China, had a particular fondness for investing in the arts and culture industry. For example, next year he would pour money into directors like Old Mouzi to open an arts development company. Later, he also invested in Legendary Pictures and so on.

Zhou Quan liked to invest in finance and consumer goods, such as CreditEase and Bosideng.

Lin Dongliang preferred to invest in the internet industry, like NetDragon, SouFun, 91 Assistant, UCWeb, and so on. This man had also been a think tank member for the State Council's Development Research Center.

"Swish!"

Xiong Xiaoge swung his club. "That Tsinghua junior of yours is probably going to take a tumble this time."

Lin Dongliang smiled. "He's met an interesting opponent. Yesterday, Xiaonei announced that its registered users surpassed 700,000. That's growing way too fast."

"You're paying so much attention. Thinking of investing in Xiaonei?" Zhou Quan asked.

Lin Dongliang said, "Still observing."

"If you're going to invest, do it early. The founder of Xiaonei is not a bad investment target," Zhou Quan said.

Li Chunsheng said, "Profitability for that kind of model is always a problem. A Series B financing round might not be easy."

Lin Dongliang said, "I heard someone in the US valued Facebook at 50 million US dollars. But their founding team isn't satisfied and is still negotiating. But hey, that's just a rumor. You have to judge for yourself whether to believe it."

Li Chunsheng was a bit conflicted. If Facebook could secure such a high valuation, then Xiaonei, as a similar product, wouldn't have to worry about a second round of financing, regardless of its profitability.

But if he kept waiting to see the trend in the US, he would miss the best opportunity to invest in Xiaonei.

The three played a few more strokes. Li Chunsheng said, "I want to make contact with this person first. If he's reliable, I'll invest early."

He invested in people, not companies.

Because in the wave of internet startups, there were too many monsters and demons. A perfectly good project might grow very rapidly in its early stages, only to be ruined because the founder self-destructed.

With a light push of the club, the golf ball went into the hole. Li Chunsheng said, "Next week I'll go to Beijing to personally observe Zheng Zhihao and his team!"

Beijing, recording studio.

Today, the official recording for "The Wind Rises" began. Bian Guanyue also had to record the song she had written.

Li Jian had come uninvited, and he brought along people from TEDA Audio & Video.

They wanted to buy "The Wind Rises."

"Selling the song is impossible," Zheng Zhihao refused outright. "I said I'd give it to Li Jian to sing, but that's only giving him the performance rights and the corresponding rights for his next album. And, a time limit must be specified."

This meant that within the period stipulated by the licensing agreement, Li Jian could perform this song on various occasions. He could also include this song in his next album. When the contract expired, the corresponding rights would automatically revert. No sub-licensing was permitted.

The performance rights also had a time limit. For example, if it was only licensed for ten years, then if Li Jian performed it eleven years later, he would have to pay Zheng Zhiwu for each performance.

The person TEDA Audio & Video sent over was named Tang Daosheng. He said, in a normal negotiating tone, "Mr. Chen, piracy is rampant these days. Especially online, a certain Baidu MP3 is the biggest music pirate. If you sell the song to us, we can't do anything about online piracy, but we can do our best to prevent it in the physical world."

"You can sell it to us as a one-time buyout, or you can collect royalties based on album sales, just like how you published 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty.' We can also help you manage online and wireless value-added services, like ringback tones. That can earn a lot of money!"

Zheng Zhiwu turned to ask Bian Guanyue, "Guanguan, what do you think?"

"You decide." Bian Guanyue just wanted to record the song quickly.

Zheng Zhiwu smiled at Kong Yongwen and said, "I'm not short on money. Of course, for the wireless value-added services, we can discuss that separately. It's fine if you don't want to cooperate. Many others will come knocking."

Tang Daosheng didn't want to negotiate anymore.

But Li Jian wanted the song and frantically made eye signals at Kong Yongwen.

Kong Yongwen was helpless. "Alright, let's do as you say. Let's talk about the wireless value-added services..."

"No rush for now. Let's talk after the song is released," Zheng Zhiwu cut him off directly.

What was the point of talking now? Once the song became a hit, it would be a different price.

Tang Daosheng sighed. "When do we sign the licensing agreement?"

This licensing agreement was the so-called "giving the song": allowing Li Jian to perform it commercially and include it in his next album. But the license had a time limit. During the license period, Zheng Zhiwu wouldn't collect any money. It was equivalent to Li Jian singing this song as an advertisement for Xiaonei, and he had to mention Xiaonei during the recording.

The better Li Jian's album sold, the more people would know about Xiaonei.

Zheng Zhiwu said, "You guys set the time. I'll have a lawyer review the contract. You'll pay the lawyer's fees."

"Thank you. It's a pleasure working with you." Kong Yong smiled and shook his hand. He had wanted to accept from the beginning, but was held back by the record company.

Bian Guanyue was already going in to record her song.

Li Jian was chatting with Zheng Zhihao. "Your three-line poems really gave the Tsinghua alumni a beating."

"Haha, you know about Zhanshow too?" Zheng Zhiwu asked.

Li Jian said with a smile, "It's spread all over the Tsinghua alumni circles in Beijing. Some are even calling it the great Tsinghua-Peking University internet war, saying you toppled our senior."

Zhanshow was in an even worse state than 5Q Campus.

The former was beaten to death in its kindergarten stage, while the latter was left crippled in its cradle.

However, Zhang Fan was still struggling to keep Zhanshow afloat. He believed that with his connections to the government, businesses, and universities, and with the powerful tool of Yiyou Mail, he could slowly increase his user base, bit by bit.

In another timeline, even after being battered by Xiaonei like this, he still managed to keep Zhanshow running past 2010.

Li Jian said, "The three-line poems are actually very interesting. I've seen many excellent ones collected by netizens, and there are two that I'm thinking of expanding into songs."

At this time, Li Jian actually used the internet. Twenty years later, he wouldn't even touch it. During the pandemic, he carried an old-fashioned mobile phone and couldn't scan QR codes, so he had to carry a tablet with him...

"I also like to write poetry. Perhaps we can collaborate again someday," Zheng Zhiwu said.

Businessmen always collaborate with celebrities. At least with Li Jian, he wouldn't have to worry about a scandal.

Kong Yongwen just sat there waiting, chatting with Li Jian until Bian Guanyue finished recording her song.

The second step of the plan could begin.
